title: New Authority Checklist 4: Show Me The Money (Invoicing & Factoring)
body_text: Step 4: Decide how you’ll get paid One important thing to understand as you start your carrier operations is that most customers (brokers and shippers) do not pay the moment you deliver. Most brokers have Net 30 payment terms. This means that if you deliver a load on January 1st, you won’t get paid until January 31st. Brokers face the same issue with shippers: many shippers do not pay for 60-90 days until after the load has been delivered. Usually, the larger the shipper, the longer their payment terms. If you take it one step further, shippers actually face the same issue with consumers. Let’s say Walmart sells an item to a customer on January 1st. Walmart actually incurred the costs to manufacture and transport the item many months ago. This means that nearly every player in the logistics industry needs to finance their working capital. The larger players raise debt facilities. Many small carriers use factoring companies, to get paid as soon as they deliver. Understanding factoring Factoring companies do the following for their carrier customers: They pay you as soon as you send acceptable proof of delivery for a load They vet the creditworthiness of brokers They handle all collections operations (sending invoices, chasing late payments, reconciling incoming deposits with invoices) Factoring allows you to sell your unpaid invoices to a factoring company at a discounted rate, giving you immediate access to cash. The process is simple: once you deliver a load, instead of waiting for weeks or even months for the payment, you send the paperwork to a factoring company. They will verify the authenticity and legitimacy before offering you a percentage of the invoice's value upfront. Most factoring companies deposit cash to your account within 24-48 hours for a 2-4% fee. In addition to the obvious service of upfront cash payment, factoring companies handle all collections operations on behalf of their carrier customers. This saves carriers time spent chasing down late payments and handling collections efforts. Additionally, most factoring companies take on the risk of vetting brokers for creditworthiness. In these contracts, if a broker goes out of business, but the factoring company approved you to factor a load from that broker, the factoring company will pay the expected invoice. How to invoice brokers directly Many carriers choose to save the 2-4% and manage cash flow themselves. If you choose to invoice brokers directly, you would follow the steps below: 0. Create your standard invoice template Since your bank remit information does not change from load to load, you can create a standard invoice template to use for all loads. You can use our Invoice Template or create your own. 1. Record billing details For each broker you book a load with, record how, where, and when they require you to bill them for the load. You can find billing details on the Rate Confirmation document. Most brokers will require the invoice sent to a specific email address. A few will require you to download a separate app and upload the paperwork to their portal, or even to mail the documents via physical mail. 2. Assemble your “invoice packet” Once you deliver, you’ll want to have the following documents ready: the signed Rate Confirmation, Proof of Delivery, and the Invoice. Many brokers will delay or withhold payment if they deem the Proof of Delivery to be incomplete in any way. To make sure they 3. Send the invoice Most brokers require that you email them the invoice packet, so we’ll outline the standard email here: Subject: Invoice for load # [load number on RateCon], MC[your MC#] Body : Reference the load number and your MC number again Attachments : RateCon, POD, and Invoice, all as separate PDFs or as a single PDF 4. Follow up the moment the invoice is overdue Many brokers need this extra step. We recommend that you include a copy of the original invoice for reference. ‍ Continue the New Authority Checklist series below: New Authority Checklist 1: First Things First (Business Setup) New Authority Checklist 2: Choose Your Player (Equipment) New Authority Checklist 3: Cover Your Assets (Insurance) ‍ About TrueNorth TrueNorth pioneers a new era for truckers, new carriers, and owner-operators. Born from a legacy of trucking roots, it transforms the industry's landscape with a cutting-edge operating system. By replacing outdated processes with a unified mobile app, TrueNorth empowers truckers with superpowers – a dispatcher, CRM, financial dashboard, and real-time market insights. Bridging the gap between traditional fleets and tech companies, TrueNorth champions truckers' profitability, offering tools, and support for streamlined operations. In a world where autonomy looms, TrueNorth remains the ally ensuring profits and efficiency for the heroes steering the wheels of commerce. Get started with TrueNorth today , and see how a trucker-first tech platform can revolutionize your operations.

title: CVSA Inspections: Understanding and Preparing for Them
body_text: The Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance ( CVSA ) is a nonprofit association made up of various governmental (local, state, federal, provincial, and territorial) officials and industry representatives. The CVSA makes recommendations that are designed to provide common standards for roadside inspections in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Those standards are used by safety inspectors. The CVSA also certifies safety inspectors. None of us love to go through inspections of any kind, but roadside inspections benefit all of us and our safety by making sure equipment is in good working order and drivers are complying with hours-of-service regulations. Similar to an annual medical exam, this process is somewhat unpleasant, but important for long-term health. There are eight different inspection levels. Refer to a previous blog post, How to Stay DOT Compliant , for an outline of those roadside and non-roadside inspections. Another blog post, FMCSA New Entrant Audits , describes the things all new carriers can expect during their initial audit. That is a good place to start to make sure you have a solid foundation and are prepared for future inspections. The most common inspections are Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3. These inspections can be performed at any time and do not require advance notice. What Leads To Inspections? There are a variety of reasons that inspections occur. Often, there is no particular reason a certain vehicle or driver is selected to be inspected. The inspectors have a job to do, and your vehicle was in the right place at the right time (or, perhaps not) to be selected. It happens at random. The selections do not always happen by chance, though. If an inspector notices something that does not look right, such as a broken headlight, then your vehicle can also be selected. The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) uses the Inspection Selection System (ISS) - a compilation of data on carriers and information in its SAFER database - to screen which carriers should be selected for an inspection. Previous inspection problems, other safety issues, or the need to get data on a carrier can all lead the ISS to flag a carrier for inspection. This means that if it has been a long time since the last inspection or if previous inspections have not gone well, the odds of another inspection occurring soon is increased. However, whether your vehicle is chosen for a reason or by chance, the most important thing is that you're prepared. Level 1 Inspections The Level 1 North American Standard Inspection is very comprehensive. It includes a review of the driver's paperwork and a complete inspection of the vehicle. Any paperwork related to operating the vehicle, or any part of the vehicle itself, is subject to inspection. This can include any or all of the following items - Paperwork: Commercial Driver's License (CDL) Medical Examiner's Certificate Skill Performance Evaluation (SPE) Certificate (if applicable) Alcohol and drugs Driver's record of duty status Hours of service Vehicle inspection report(s) Physical: Seat belt Brake systems Cargo securement Coupling devices Driveline/driveshaft Electrical cables and systems in engine and battery compartments Exhaust systems Frames Fuel systems Lighting devices (headlamps, tail lamps, stop lamps, turn signals and lamps/flags on projecting loads) Steering mechanisms Suspensions Tires Van and open-top trailer bodies Wheels, rims and hubs Windshield wipers Below is the guidance from the CVSA for inspectors doing Level 1 inspections: Choose the Inspection Site Approach the Vehicle Greet and Prepare the Driver Interview Driver Collect the Driver's Documents Check for Presence of Hazardous Materials/Dangerous Goods Identify the Carrier Examine Driver's License or CDL Check Medical Examiner's Certificate and Skill Performance Evaluation (SPE) Certificate (if applicable) Check Record of Duty Status Review Driver's Daily Vehicle Inspection Report (if applicable) Review Periodic Inspection Report(s) Prepare Driver for Vehicle Inspection Inspect Front of Tractor Inspect Left Front side of Tractor Inspect Left Saddle Tank Area Inspect Trailer Front Inspect Left Rear Tractor Area Inspect Left Side of Trailer Inspect Left Rear Trailer Wheels Inspect Rear of Trailer Inspect Double, Triple and Full Trailers Inspect Right Rear Trailer Wheels Inspect Right Side of Trailer Inspect Right Rear Tractor Area Inspect Right Saddle Tank Area Inspect Right Front Side of Tractor Inspect Steering Axle(s) Inspect Axle(s) 2 and/or 3 Inspect Axle(s) 4 and/or 5 Prepare the Vehicle and Check Brake Adjustment Inspect Tractor Protection System (this procedure tests both the tractor protection system and the emergency brakes) Inspect Required Brake System Warning Devices Test Air Loss Rate Check Steering Wheel Lash Check Fifth Wheel Movement Complete the Inspection The time to complete the Level 1 inspection is up to 60 minutes. Level 2 Inspections The Level 2 North American Standard Inspection is basically the paperwork portion of the Level 2 plus a visual (walk-around) of the equipment. The inspector does not go under the tractor or trailer. It is possible, however, that if the inspector sees something amiss (such as fluids leaking), that the inspection could be changed to become a Level 1. The time to complete the Level 2 inspection is up to 30 minutes. Level 3 Inspections The Level 3 North American Standard Inspection includes reviewing the paperwork but nothing physical (except the seat belt). This is basically a "driver paperwork" review. The time to complete the Level 3 inspection is up to 15 minutes. CVSA Decals Successfully completing a Level 1 inspection makes the vehicle eligible for a CVSA decal. This decal applies only to the vehicle, not the driver. The decals are valid for up to three months. The CVSA decal does not guarantee that another inspection will occur during the period it is valid, but unless it is flagged for a specific reason, it is much less likely. Resources and Preparation The link to the "North American Standard Roadside Inspection Vehicle Cheat Sheet" on the CVSA resources page will pull up a one-page summary with a listing of key items to check. This helpful flyer reviews common areas of concern for inspectors. The best way to pass an inspection is to be prepared for it. Having your paperwork (or electronic equivalent) organized goes a long way to helping the inspector verify that your proverbial ducks are in a row. Inspecting and maintaining your equipment (with the paperwork to prove it) should be standard procedure. Doing poorly on a roadside inspection can lead to a CSA intervention. The FMCSA calls its safety compliance and enforcement system the Compliance, Safety, Accountability (CSA) Program . No carrier wants to participate in an intervention because they occur when the FMCSA thinks a carrier's safety performance indicates a potential safety risk. CSA Interventions include three categories: Early Contact. This involves warning letters and targeted roadside inspections. Investigation. This includes offsite and onsite detailed comprehensive reviews. Follow-On. Four basic results are most common. Cooperative Safety Plan (CSP). This involves a voluntary plan to address any safety issues. At this point, it is the best option. Notice of Violation (NOV). A formal notice but no civil penalties. Corrective actions must be taken to correct the violations. Notice of Claim (NOC). Violations warrant civil penalties. Operation Out of Service Order (OOSO). Prohibits carrier from operating, effective immediately. The best way to avoid any CSA Interventions is to do your due diligence on the front end as described above. It's important to note that inspectors are people, too, just like you and me. Sometimes we experience harder days than others. A driver's attitude while working with an inspector can make the process go more smoothly. After all, H. Jackson Brown, Jr. says, "The best preparation for tomorrow is doing your best today." body_text: Coates Joins From ECAM, a GardaWorld Company, Where He Led U.S. Sales Across Critical Infrastructure, Commercial Real Estate and Retail Appointment Strengthens Commercial Organization to Support Expansion Across Enterprise Markets PALO ALTO, Calif., Aug. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cloudastructure, Inc. ("Cloudastructure" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: CSAI), a leader in cloud-native AI surveillance and remote guarding, today announced the appointment of Nile Coates as Chief Revenue Officer. Coates will lead the Company's global sales organization, revenue operations and channel partner strategy, reporting directly to Chief Executive Officer and Chairman James McCormick. In this role, Coates will lead the expansion of Cloudastructure's commercial organization as the Company continues to broaden its presence across enterprise markets, including commercial real estate, data centers, logistics, retail and critical infrastructure. His mandate includes scaling the sales organization, strengthening channel partnerships and accelerating Cloudastructure's land-and-expand strategy within existing customer portfolios. Coates succeeds Lauren O’Brien, who has departed the Company. "Over the past several years, we've demonstrated that our platform resonates across a growing number of enterprise markets. The opportunity in front of us is no longer proving the technology. It is scaling the commercial organization capable of capturing it," said James McCormick, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Cloudastructure. title: Zoho Desk Pricing in 2026: How Much Does Zoho Desk Really Cost
summary: Zoho Desk presents itself as one of the most affordable help desk options on the market. The headline pricing looks attractive: a genuine free tier for up to three agents, and paid plans starting at just $7 per agent monthly. But the reality of what your organization will actually spend
body_text: Zoho Desk presents itself as one of the most affordable help desk options on the market. The headline pricing looks attractive: a genuine free tier for up to three agents, and paid plans starting at just $7 per agent monthly. But the reality of what your organization will actually spend depends on factors that rarely appear in the marketing materials. For IT teams, HR departments, and internal support operations evaluating help desk software, understanding the complete cost picture matters more than comparing sticker prices. The gap between what Zoho Desk advertises and what companies actually pay can reach 40% or more once you factor in telephony, storage, automation tools, and analytics add-ons. Organizations running internal support through Slack-native ticketing face an additional consideration: whether the platform integrates with existing workflows or forces employees to adopt entirely new interfaces. This breakdown covers every pricing tier, the hidden costs that inflate your total investment, how Zoho Desk compares to alternatives, and which scenarios actually justify the platform versus when simpler solutions deliver better results. Key Takeaways Zoho Desk offers five pricing tiers ranging from free to $40 per agent per month on annual billing, making it roughly 60-75% cheaper than enterprise alternatives like Zendesk, though feature availability varies significantly across tiers Hidden costs can substantially increase your total spend beyond advertised per-agent fees, including telephony through Zoho Voice, which offers a Basic plan at $34 per user monthly or a Standard plan at $49 per admin plus 10 telephony agents (billed annually), storage overages, and premium analytics packages Full AI capabilities require the Enterprise tier at $40 per agent with bundled pricing that eliminates per-resolution fees, with comparative data suggesting approximately 90% savings compared to competitors charging per AI interaction at high volumes Implementation typically takes 1-8 weeks depending on complexity due to a steeper learning curve than simpler alternatives, with users consistently noting the text-heavy interface requires more training Slack-native teams may find better value elsewhere since Zoho Desk requires a separate web interface, creating context-switching friction that purpose-built messaging platform solutions eliminate entirely Understanding Zoho Desk's Tiered Pricing Model Zoho Desk structures its pricing across five distinct tiers, each targeting different organizational sizes and feature requirements. The model follows a per-agent, per-month approach with significant savings for annual billing, typically 30-50% compared to monthly payment options. Current Zoho Desk Pricing Tiers: Free Plan: $0 for up to 3 agents, includes email ticketing, basic help center, and standard reports Express Plan: $7 per agent monthly on annual billing ($9 monthly), capped at 5 agents maximum, adds social media channels, web forms, and basic workflows Standard Plan: $14 per agent monthly on annual billing ($17 monthly), unlimited agents, includes live chat, WhatsApp integration, Answer Bot, and automation capabilities Professional Plan: $23 per agent monthly on annual billing ($35 monthly), adds telephony integration, Zia AI features, Blueprints for process automation, and multi-department support Enterprise Plan: $40 per agent monthly on annual billing ($50 monthly), includes full Zia AI suite, live chat via SalesIQ, multi-brand support, and sandbox environments Understanding Tier Limitations The Express plan carries a hard cap of 5 agents, forcing an upgrade the moment you add a sixth team member. This creates a significant cost jump for growing teams since moving from Express to Standard more than doubles your per-agent cost while removing the agent ceiling. VAT and GST charges will be added on top of listed prices (for example, 19% in Germany), a detail often overlooked when comparing against competitors who may quote tax-inclusive pricing. For organizations operating internationally, this can meaningfully impact budget projections. The free tier represents one of Zoho Desk's strongest competitive advantages. Unlike competitors who offer time-limited trials, Zoho provides genuine free-forever access for small teams. However, the features available at this tier make it suitable only for the most basic email ticketing needs without automation, AI capabilities, or multi-channel support. Breaking Down Zoho Desk Features by Price Point Understanding exactly what each tier delivers helps IT leaders and internal support managers avoid paying for capabilities they will not use or finding themselves locked out of features they need. Core Features vs. Advanced Functionality Free Tier Capabilities: Email-based ticketing with basic ticket management Public help center for self-service documentation Standard reports and dashboards Mobile application access Limited to 3 agents with no workflow automation Standard Tier Additions ($14/agent): Live chat widget deployment WhatsApp Business integration Answer Bot for basic deflection SLA management and escalation rules Workflow automation with triggers and actions Custom ticket fields and layouts Professional Tier Additions ($23/agent): Telephony through Zoho Voice integration Zia AI for sentiment analysis and predictions Blueprint visual workflow builder Multi-department ticket routing Round-robin ticket assignment Custom scheduled reports Enterprise Tier Additions ($40/agent): Full Zia AI suite with unlimited resolutions Live chat via Zoho SalesIQ Multi-brand help center support Sandbox environment for testing Custom functions and API extensions Data sharing rules across departments Hidden Costs of Feature Access The feature matrix tells only part of the story. Several capabilities that appear included actually require separate purchases or carry usage-based charges that compound over time. Telephony requires Zoho Voice: Even at Professional tier where telephony "unlocks," you must separately subscribe to Zoho Voice, which offers a Basic plan at $34 per user monthly or a Standard plan at $49 per admin plus 10 telephony agents (billed annually), plus per-minute calling charges. For a 10-agent team needing phone support, this adds $4,080+ annually to your Zoho Desk costs. Analytics at scale needs Zoho Analytics: While basic reporting comes included, cross-module reporting and advanced analytics require Zoho Analytics, priced at $24-455 monthly depending on user count and data volume. Automation task limits exist: Zoho Flow, which powers extended automations beyond Zoho Desk's built-in capabilities, includes 1,000 tasks monthly before usage fees kick in. Heavy automation users may see $10-120 monthly in additional charges. The Real Cost of Zoho Desk: Beyond the Sticker Price Calculating total cost of ownership requires looking past per-agent licensing to include implementation, training, ongoing maintenance, and the productivity impact of platform complexity. Calculating TCO for a 10-Agent Team A realistic first-year cost projection for a 10-agent team on Zoho Desk Professional tier: Direct Licensing Costs: Base license: $2,760 annually (10 agents × $23 × 12 months, annual billing) Zia AI: Included at Professional tier (basic features only) Add-On Costs: Zoho Voice telephony: $4,080+ annually Storage overages (estimated): $240 annually Zoho Analytics (optional): $288-1,200 annually Implementation Costs: Setup and configuration: $500-1,000 (industry estimate) Team training: $500-1,000 (industry estimate) Integration development: Variable based on requirements Realistic First-Year Total: $8,080-10,660 This calculation reveals that a team expecting to pay $2,760 for help desk software may actually spend 3-4x that amount once telephony, analytics, and implementation factor in. Unexpected Expenses to Budget For Monthly vs. Annual Billing Premium: Organizations requiring monthly flexibility pay 30-50% more than annual rates. For a 10-agent Professional deployment, this means $4,200 annually on monthly billing versus $2,760 on annual commitment. Light Agent Fees: Read-only access for stakeholders who need ticket visibility but not full agent capabilities costs approximately $6 per user monthly at Professional and Enterprise tiers. Storage Expansion: Base storage allocations run out quickly for teams handling high ticket volumes with attachments. Overages cost roughly $4 per GB monthly . For example, one blog estimates that a 20-person team using Zoho One (which includes Desk) found their effective cost reached $52.40 per user versus the advertised $37, representing a 42% increase from hidden expenses including storage, Flow automation, and support tier upgrades. Evaluating Value: Is Zoho Desk Right for Your Needs? Zoho Desk delivers strong value in specific scenarios while creating unnecessary complexity in others. Understanding where the platform excels helps organizations avoid expensive mismatches. When Zoho Desk Makes Sense Budget-constrained external customer support: For organizations handling primarily email and social media customer inquiries, Zoho Desk Standard at $14 per agent provides multi-channel capabilities at 60-75% lower cost than enterprise alternatives. Deep Zoho ecosystem commitment: Teams already using Zoho CRM, Books, and Analytics benefit from native integrations that eliminate sync lag and reduce implementation time. The unified data layer across Zoho products creates efficiencies that standalone help desks cannot match. High-volume AI requirements: Organizations processing 10,000+ conversations monthly save substantially with Zoho's bundled AI model. At Enterprise tier, unlimited AI resolutions cost approximately $9,600 annually for 20 agents, compared to $118,800+ for per-resolution competitors at the same volume. When to Consider Alternatives Slack or Teams-centric organizations: If your workforce already lives in messaging platforms, forcing them into a separate web application creates adoption friction that compounds over time. Purpose-built Slack support solutions eliminate context switching entirely. Internal support and employee help desk: Zoho Desk's architecture optimizes for external customer service workflows. IT, HR, and employee support teams handling internal requests often find the interface over-engineered for their needs while lacking features specific to internal operations. Speed-to-value priority: Implementation typically takes 1-8 weeks depending on complexity due to interface complexity and training requirements. Teams needing help desk capabilities operational in days rather than weeks should evaluate simpler alternatives. Non-technical administrators: The platform's steep learning curve demands more sophisticated admin capabilities than modern alternatives. Marketing ops, sales operations, and HR teams without dedicated technical resources often struggle with ongoing configuration changes. AI and Automation in Zoho Desk: Budget Impact Analysis AI capabilities increasingly drive help desk purchasing decisions, but pricing models vary dramatically across vendors. Understanding how Zoho Desk's approach compares helps organizations project realistic costs at their expected volume. Zoho's Bundled AI Model vs. Per-Resolution Pricing Zoho Desk bundles its full Zia AI suite at Enterprise tier ($40/agent) with no additional per-resolution charges. This creates significant cost advantages at scale but requires the highest pricing tier to access meaningful AI capabilities. Comparative AI Costs at 10,000 Monthly Conversations: Zoho Desk Enterprise (20 agents): Approximately $9,600 annually (flat rate, unlimited resolutions) Per-resolution competitors: $118,800+ annually at $0.99 per resolution Per-agent plus per-resolution models: $192,000+ annually The comparative data suggesting approximately 90% savings at high volumes makes Zoho Desk's bundled approach attractive for organizations certain they will leverage AI extensively. However, teams with lower volumes may find they are paying for AI capabilities they rarely use at the Enterprise tier. Measuring ROI on Help Desk AI Zoho Desk does not publish official resolution rate benchmarks for Zia AI. Competitor transparency varies, with some platforms claiming 65% resolution rates in marketing materials. For internal support operations, AI value extends beyond simple deflection metrics: Documentation automation: Does the AI generate help articles from resolved tickets, or does your team manually maintain knowledge bases? Intelligent routing: Can the system route tickets based on content analysis, or does it rely on manual triage? Workflow triggering: Does AI initiate actions in connected systems like provisioning access or updating HR records? Self-learning knowledge bases that automatically detect repeat questions and generate draft articles deliver compounding value over time, reducing both ticket volume and documentation maintenance burden. Integrating Zoho Desk with Your Business Tools Help desk software exists within a broader technology ecosystem. Integration capabilities determine whether the platform amplifies your existing investments or creates data silos requiring manual reconciliation. Zoho's Ecosystem Advantage Zoho Desk's strongest integration story involves other Zoho products. Organizations using three or more Zoho applications benefit from: Zoho CRM: Unified customer records, deal context within tickets, and shared timeline across sales and support Zoho Books: Financial context including invoice status and payment history visible to support agents Zoho Analytics: Cross-module reporting connecting support metrics to business outcomes Zoho SalesIQ: Live chat with visitor tracking and proactive engagement Third-Party Integration Limitations Outside the Zoho ecosystem, integration breadth narrows considerably. Zoho Desk offers 200+ integrations compared to 1,500+ for enterprise competitors. This gap matters most for organizations using: Non-Zoho CRM platforms (Salesforce, HubSpot) Project management tools outside the Zoho suite Communication platforms like Slack or Microsoft Teams HRIS systems for employee directory synchronization Native Slack integration through purpose-built platforms eliminates the need for third-party connectors, app marketplace add-ons, or custom development to achieve two-way ticket synchronization. For teams evaluating integration requirements, the question becomes whether Zoho's ecosystem depth compensates for its narrower third-party breadth. Zoho Desk for Small Business vs. Enterprise: Scaling Considerations Pricing tier selection depends heavily on current team size, growth trajectory, and feature requirements. The economics shift substantially as organizations scale. Small Business Considerations (Under 25 Agents) The Express tier's $7 per agent pricing looks attractive but carries the 5-agent ceiling that forces upgrades quickly. Small teams should calculate: Path 1: Start at Express, upgrade later 5 agents at Express: $420 annually Growth to 6 agents forces Standard: $1,008 annually (140% increase) Hidden cost: Migration effort and retraining Path 2: Start at Standard 5 agents at Standard: $840 annually Growth to 10 agents: $1,680 annually (proportional scaling) Benefit: No forced migration, access to automation from day one For teams confident they will exceed 5 agents within 12-18 months, starting at Standard often proves more cost-effective than the apparent savings of Express. Enterprise-Grade Requirements and Costs Large organizations evaluating Zoho Desk Enterprise should factor in: SSO and security: Enterprise tier includes SSO, but HIPAA compliance with BAAs requires custom arrangements Scale limitations: While theoretically unlimited, the platform's architecture optimizes for mid-market rather than enterprise scale Support tiers: Enterprise support with industry-leading SLAs requires additional investment beyond licensing 50-Agent TCO Comparison: At the 50-agent scale, Zoho Desk Enterprise runs approximately $49,400-61,400 for year one including implementation and telephony, representing 60%+ savings versus enterprise alternatives. However, organizations with internal support use cases concentrated in Slack or Teams should evaluate whether purpose-built solutions deliver better value through: Faster implementation (days versus weeks) Lower training overhead (native to existing workflows) Simpler administration as requirements evolve Workflow automation spanning IT, HR, finance, and workplace operations Zoho Desk vs. Unthread: Comparing Modern Workflow Approaches The fundamental difference between Zoho Desk and Slack-native platforms comes down to where your team already works versus where traditional help desks force them to go. How Slack-Native Solutions Impact Costs Zoho Desk operates as a standalone web application that requires agents to maintain a separate browser tab or window, logging in and out throughout their workday. For internal support teams whose employees already communicate through Slack, this creates measurable friction: Context switching overhead: Agents toggle between Slack conversations and Zoho Desk constantly Training investment: New team members must learn an entirely separate interface Adoption challenges: Employees must remember to submit requests through the help desk rather than simply messaging colleagues Purpose-built Slack ticketing eliminates these friction points by converting existing Slack channels into structured help desks. A channel like #it-help becomes the single intake point for employee requests, with tickets created automatically from messages. Some request types can remain visible in-channel while sensitive matters route to private DMs or confidential flows. The Value of Purpose-Built AI Agents for Internal Support Zoho Desk's Zia AI provides sentiment analysis, reply suggestions, and basic automation at Enterprise tier. However, the system requires manual knowledge base construction and ongoing curation to function effectively. Improve Your Internal Support Processes with Unthread Unthread's agentic AI takes a different approach, automatically learning from resolved tickets to generate documentation without manual content creation by understanding request intent and referencing the self-learning knowledge base. Key differentiators for internal support: Bring-your-own-LLM capability: Organizations can use their own GPT instances via MCP integration rather than being locked into a vendor's AI Broader automation scope: While some platforms primarily automate access requests, Unthread supports workflows across IT service desk operations, HR ticketing , finance, procurement, and workplace operations Configuration simplicity: Setup takes days rather than weeks, with lower ongoing admin overhead as workflows, routing rules, and automations change Stop making employees switch tools just to get help. Unthread turns Slack conversations into structured support tickets and can get your help desk up and running in days instead of the 1–8 weeks typical of a Zoho Desk implementation. Sign up for a demo . Frequently Asked Questions How does Zoho Desk handle multi-language support, and does it affect pricing? Zoho Desk provides multi-language help center support at Professional tier and above, allowing organizations to create knowledge base content in multiple languages. The platform supports interface localization for agents as well. However, AI capabilities like Zia function primarily in English, with limited support for other languages. Organizations requiring robust multi-language AI interactions should verify language-specific capabilities during evaluation. There are no additional per-language fees, but the functionality differences between English and other languages may impact usefulness for global teams. Can Zoho Desk handle private or confidential ticket types for HR-sensitive requests? Zoho Desk supports department-based access controls and private ticket visibility settings at Professional tier and above. However, the platform was not designed specifically for HR use cases involving highly sensitive employee matters. Ticket visibility depends on department configuration and agent permissions rather than specialized privacy workflows. Organizations handling confidential HR requests like payroll disputes, harassment reports, or medical accommodations should evaluate whether general-purpose access controls meet their compliance and privacy requirements, or whether purpose-built HR ticketing solutions provide stronger guarantees. What happens to my data if I downgrade from a higher Zoho Desk tier? Downgrading from a higher tier restricts access to features but does not automatically delete associated data. However, data created using tier-specific features like Blueprint workflows, custom fields beyond lower-tier limits, or advanced analytics becomes inaccessible until you upgrade again. Zoho recommends exporting critical data before downgrading. The platform provides data export capabilities, but complex configurations and automation rules do not transfer cleanly between tiers. Organizations should test downgrade scenarios in sandbox environments before committing to tier changes that might disrupt operations. How does Zoho Desk's mobile app compare to the desktop experience for field agents? Zoho Desk's mobile applications for iOS and Android provide core ticket management, knowledge base access, and basic reporting. However, advanced features like Blueprint automation, detailed analytics, and complex ticket workflows function better on desktop. Field agents can view and respond to tickets, access customer history, and update ticket status, but creating sophisticated automation or generating detailed reports requires the web interface. Teams with primarily mobile agents should evaluate whether the mobile experience supports their critical workflows or creates friction that impacts response times. Does Zoho Desk offer any nonprofit or educational discounts? Zoho provides nonprofit pricing across its product suite, including Desk, though specific discount percentages are not publicly listed. Organizations must apply and verify nonprofit status to receive adjusted pricing. Educational institutions may qualify for similar programs. Discounts typically apply to paid tiers rather than the free plan, and eligibility requirements vary by region. Nonprofits should contact Zoho sales directly with documentation to receive accurate pricing quotes rather than assuming specific discount levels based on other vendors' programs.

title: Cosmic Rundown: OpenAI Attacks Hugging Face, DeepSeek V4 Arrives, Memory Sells Out
summary: Daily developer news: OpenAI accidentally attacks Hugging Face. DeepSeek V4 Flash launches. 2027 memory sold out. Gentoo closes bug tracker due to AI scrapers.
body_text: OpenAI's accidental attack on Hugging Face Simon Willison documented the full timeline of OpenAI's accidental attack against Hugging Face , piecing together how automated systems from one AI company overwhelmed infrastructure at another. The Hacker News discussion explored the broader implications: as AI systems become more autonomous, the line between aggressive crawling and denial-of-service attacks becomes harder to draw. Rate limiting and robots.txt are suggestions, not enforcement mechanisms. For teams running public APIs or content platforms, this is a reminder that traffic from AI systems does not follow the same patterns as human users. A single misconfigured crawler can generate more load than thousands of real visitors. DeepSeek V4 Flash ships DeepSeek released V4 Flash 0731 , their latest model optimized for speed. The ARC Prize results page shows benchmark performance against other models. The discussion compared V4 Flash to competing offerings. Flash variants trade some capability for latency, which matters for applications where response time affects user experience directly. Content platforms that integrate AI generation benefit from faster models. Lower latency means editors can iterate more quickly, and automated workflows complete faster. Cosmic's AI agents can work with multiple model providers, so teams can choose the right speed-capability tradeoff for each use case. 2027 memory capacity already sold out IGN reported that 2027 memory capacity is already sold out , continuing what some are calling "RAMageddon." AI training and inference workloads are consuming memory production capacity years in advance. The thread discussed what this means for hardware planning. Teams building AI infrastructure need to think about memory constraints as a first-order concern, not an afterthought. Gentoo closes Bugzilla due to AI scraper overload Gentoo maintainer mgorny announced that Bugzilla had to be closed because AI bot scrapers were overwhelming the service. The discussion documented similar experiences from other open source projects. This pattern keeps repeating: AI companies training models scrape everything they can reach, and smaller infrastructure cannot handle the load. Projects that serve public APIs or documentation need defensive measures that were not necessary even two years ago. DeepMind's WeatherNext forecasts cyclones DeepMind published details on WeatherNext achieving breakthrough cyclone forecasting . The model predicts cyclone formation and paths more accurately than previous approaches. The discussion explored how weather prediction has become one of the clearest success stories for large-scale AI models. The physics are well-understood, the data is abundant, and the evaluation criteria are objective. Hardware backdoors discovered in x86 CPUs Researchers published Rosenbridge , documenting hardware backdoors in some x86 CPUs. The thread discussed the security implications and which chips are affected. US Department of Energy launches Genesis Open Models The Department of Energy launched the Genesis Open Models Initiative , releasing models trained on scientific data. The discussion explored applications for research and specialized domains. Microsoft Edge follows Chrome on ad blockers Microsoft Edge is locking out older ad blockers , following Chrome's transition to Manifest V3. The thread debated whether the technical changes genuinely improve security or primarily benefit advertising revenue. Quick hits DNS for-sale specification : A new specification lets domains declare they are for sale directly in DNS . The discussion explored whether domain brokers will adopt it. Voyager 2 gets another year : NASA figured out how to keep Voyager 2 running for another year by managing power budgets. Hamster on Strava : A physicist rigged his hamster's wheel to upload to Strava . The hamster is outrunning some humans. Ancient Library : A new tool lets you click any word in Greek or Latin texts to parse it , covering 1,060 texts. Assembly Hall of Shame : A collection of cursed assembly code patterns from the same researcher who found the CPU backdoors. Building content infrastructure that adapts to these shifts requires tools designed for change. Cosmic's AI agents handle content generation with oversight built in. The REST API integrates with any model. Start building for free and see how modern content infrastructure supports the workflows these developments enable.

title: Datavault AI Will Acquire CyberCatch in an All-Cash Transaction
summary: Adding AI-Driven, Quantum-Resistant Cyber Risk Mitigation to Its Quantum-Secured Edge Platform. Data Vault® Artificial Intelligence Platform…...
body_text: Datavault AI Will Acquire CyberCatch in an All-Cash Transaction August 14, 2026 10:46am EDT Adding AI-Driven, Quantum-Resistant Cyber Risk Mitigation to Its Quantum-Secured Edge Platform. Data Vault® Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) will be enhanced with automatic cybersecurity check and resolution capabilities. PHILADELPHIA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Datavault AI Inc. (“Datavault AI” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: DVLT), a provider of data monetization, credentialing, digital engagement, and real-world asset (“RWA”) tokenization technologies, today announced they have signed a definitive agreement under which Datavault AI will acquire 100% of CyberCatch Holdings, Inc. (TSXV: CYBE) (OTCQB: CYBHF), a cybersecurity company offering a patented, AI-enabled platform for continuous compliance and cyber risk mitigation, in an all-cash transaction structured as a court-approved plan of arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia). The acquisition is expected to bring CyberCatch’s AI-enabled continuous compliance and cyber risk mitigation platform into Datavault AI’s Quantum Private Network (QPN) GPU ecosystem, addressing a global information security market that Gartner projected would reach $213 billion in 2025. Under the definitive agreement, Datavault AI will acquire all of CyberCatch’s issued and outstanding common shares, approximately 26.8 million shares, for USD $94,500,000 in cash, representing USD $3.53 per share to CyberCatch’s shareholders. All outstanding dilutive securities of CyberCatch will be exchanged on a cashless-exercise basis. Upon closing, subject to customary board, stock exchange, and any necessary regulatory and shareholder approvals, CyberCatch is expected to operate as a subsidiary of Datavault AI from San Diego, California, with CyberCatch founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer Sai Huda serving as President of the subsidiary and reporting to Nathaniel T. Bradley, CEO of Datavault AI. Strategic Rationale The combination is positioned at the intersection of two of cybersecurity’s largest secular markets. According to Gartner (2025) , worldwide end-user spending on information security was projected to reach $213 billion in 2025, underscoring the scale of the market CyberCatch’s platform is expected to serve within Datavault AI’s SanQtum-secured edge ecosystem. Threat actors are increasingly using AI to breach networks and deploy ransomware within minutes of first contact. According to CrowdStrike’s 2026 Global Threat Report , AI-enabled adversary attacks rose 89% year-over-year in 2025, and the average eCrime breakout time, the time from initial intrusion to data exfiltration, fell to 29 minutes, a 65% increase in adversary speed compared to 2024. The combination is also positioned for the post-quantum security era. Google has set 2029 as its internal deadline to migrate authentication systems to quantum-resistant cryptography, and separate Google Quantum AI research has found that the qubit threshold required to break widely used elliptic curve cryptography is an order of magnitude lower than previously estimated, suggesting the timeline for a cryptographically relevant quantum computer may be shorter than previously assumed. CyberCatch is converting its patent-pending, multi-authority, attribute-based encryption with revocation (“MARS-MABE”) technology to attain quantum resistance, and combining MARS-MABE with continuous agentic AI penetration testing is expected to create a next-generation cybersecurity stack applicable across healthcare, defense, manufacturing, financial services, and energy. About CyberCatch’s Platform and Leadership CyberCatch’s patented, AI-enabled continuous cybersecurity compliance and risk mitigation platform uses generative AI to confirm that all legally required controls are in place and to calculate a Cyber Hygiene Score, and uses agentic AI to continuously simulate threat-actor tactics, techniques, and procedures, perform penetration tests, and calculate a Cyber Breach Score. The platform is designed to detect gaps for prompt remediation before a threat actor can exploit them. The platform tests cybersecurity controls continuously from three dimensions: outside-in, inside-out, and social engineering, mapping to NIST CSF 2.0, NIST 800-171, CMMC 2.0, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and other regulated frameworks, replacing once-a-year manual penetration tests with continuous agentic AI penetration testing using specialized skill-set agents. Most companies cannot afford the human experts and time a comprehensive penetration test requires, and those that can typically perform one only once a year; a gap CyberCatch’s platform is designed to close across sectors and geographies. CyberCatch’s agentic AI solution is comprised of specialized agents with the skill sets of an attacker, each performing specific tasks such as reconnaissance, vulnerability detection, selection of attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures, vulnerability exploitation, evidence gathering, reporting, and risk mitigation recommendations. The platform provides dashboard reporting mapped to cybersecurity control failures and compliance status against frameworks such as NIST CSF 2.0, NIST 800-171, CMMC, HIPAA, CAN/DGC 104, and EU NIS, among others, for root cause analysis and targeted risk mitigation. CyberCatch’s patent-pending MARS-MABE technology is designed to provide several advantages over current RSA and AES-256 encryption, including granting data access only when fine-grained user attributes are met, limiting user access to fine-grained data subsets, and enabling instant revocation of user access to data subsets without the need to re-encrypt the entire data set, providing speed and cost savings. CyberCatch is led by founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer Sai Huda, a globally recognized cybersecurity expert, author of Next Level Cybersecurity, co-author of Canada’s National Cybersecurity Standard, and inventor of USPTO Patent No. 11,297,094, “Automated and Continuous Cybersecurity Assessment with Measurement and Scoring.” He is the former founder and CEO of Compliance Coach, which was acquired by FIS, where he served as GM, Risk, Information Security, and Compliance Solutions. title: Nordstrom Rack Return Policy: Windows, Rules & Exceptions
summary: The Nordstrom Rack return policy gives you 30 days in-store, 40 days online, and no exceptions on final sale. See what resellers need before sourcing.
body_text: If you're trying to pin down the Nordstrom Rack return policy before you buy or before you box something up, here's the short version: you get 30 days from the purchase date on anything bought in-store, and 40 days from the ship date on online or app orders. Those figures reflect Nordstrom Rack's current posted policy, which can change without notice, so confirm the exact terms on nordstromrack.com before you rely on them. Items also need to be unworn and unaltered, with the original tags still attached, and you need proof of purchase to get an actual refund instead of store credit. That's a lot stricter than full-line Nordstrom , which runs case-by-case with no fixed cutoff at all. The biggest trap in the whole policy: Nordstrom Rack final sale items are non-returnable, no exceptions, and that label is easy to miss on a packed clearance rack . Ahead, you'll find the in-store and online breakdown, what's excluded, how the Nordstrom comparison actually works, and what the return window means if you're sourcing inventory to resell. Return Windows and Conditions at a Glance Two timelines govern the Nordstrom Rack return window: 30 days from the purchase date for in-store buys, 40 days from the ship date for online and app orders. Condition requirements apply to both tracks: items need to be unworn, unaltered, with original tags on and packaging intact where it applies. Proof of purchase decides your refund. A receipt, order confirmation email, or order number gets you a refund. If you return to Nordstrom Rack without a receipt, expect manager discretion and store credit at the lowest recorded price instead. Gift receipts get you store credit only, never a refund to the original payment method. Holiday extensions aren't guaranteed every year. Rack sometimes extends a window during the holiday season, but check the official policy page each year rather than assume last year's terms still apply. In-Store Purchases In-store purchases get a firm 30 days from the purchase date, with no grace period. A day late means no refund, and you'll need to bring the item back to a physical Nordstrom Rack location, since cross-store returns to full-line Nordstrom aren't accepted. That surprises plenty of shoppers who assume the two banners share a return desk. They don't. Refunds go back to your original payment method: cash purchases get refunded in cash on the spot, while credit and debit card refunds typically take 3 to 5 business days to post. Exchanges are allowed within that same 30-day window if you'd rather swap sizes or colors than get your money back, so you don't lose that option just because you're past the halfway point. Hang onto your receipt anyway . It's the fastest way to skip a manager lookup at the counter. Online and App Purchases Online and app orders get a longer runway: 40 days measured from the ship date, not the date you placed the order. That extra 10 days accounts for transit time, so a slow carrier doesn't eat into your window. Drop it off at any Nordstrom Rack store, which processes your refund faster. Ship it back using a prepaid label generated at nordstromrack.com. Mail it back, and budget 5 to 7 business days for the warehouse to process the return once it arrives, then another 3 to 5 business days for the refund to hit your card. Original outbound shipping charges aren't refunded unless Rack made the error, like shipping the wrong item or something arriving damaged. For anyone shopping from a phone, the Rack app lets you start a return and generate a QR code for drop-off at select locations. That skips the printer entirely and speeds up the in-person option. Save the confirmation email either way. It doubles as proof of purchase if the physical receipt gets lost. What Cannot Be Returned Nordstrom Rack final sale items top the list, and this is the rule that trips up the most shoppers. They're marked on the product page and on your receipt, no exceptions, not even for a defect. If a final sale item turns out to be damaged, that's a customer service claim, not a return. Anything worn, washed, or altered Items missing their original tags Opened fragrances and opened beauty or skincare products Special-order merchandise made or sourced specifically for you Miss the return window entirely, and you're relying on a manager's approval to get anything back, which isn't guaranteed. The practical move is checking for the final sale indicator before you buy, especially on deeply discounted clearance items where the tag is easy to overlook in a crowded aisle. A quick glance at the receipt or product page before you pay saves you from owning something you can't send back. Nordstrom Rack Return Policy vs. Nordstrom: How the Policies Differ Policy Detail Nordstrom Rack Nordstrom (Full-Line) In-store return window 30 days from purchase date No set cutoff — case-by-case manager discretion Online return window 40 days from ship date No set cutoff — case-by-case Receipt required? Yes; no receipt = store credit at lowest price, manager discretion Preferred; no-receipt returns common with manager approval Final sale items Non-returnable, no exceptions Non-returnable Cross-store returns Rack only — full-line Nordstrom stores will not accept Nordstrom only — Rack stores will not accept Free return shipping (online) Yes — prepaid label via nordstromrack.com Yes — prepaid label via nordstrom.com Cardmember perks Extended terms for Icon/Ambassador Nordy Club tiers Extended terms for Icon/Ambassador Nordy Club tiers Exchanges Within same return window More flexible — handled case-by-case The comparison shoppers search for most is also the one most guides gloss over: how do Nordstrom Rack and full-line Nordstrom returns actually differ? The split is structural. The Nordstrom return policy runs on a no-hard-cutoff, case-by-case model, so there's no fixed day count and staff have real discretion to work with you. Rack enforces firm windows instead, and one rule cuts both ways: items bought at Rack cannot be returned to a full-line Nordstrom store, and Nordstrom purchases cannot be returned to Rack, period. Nordy Club Icon and Ambassador cardmembers may get extended or enhanced terms at either banner, though you should confirm current details on your account page rather than assume they carry over. Here's the side-by-side breakdown: What Resellers Should Know Before Sourcing at Nordstrom Rack Nordstrom Rack has been a reliable sourcing spot for resellers for years. Designer and contemporary labels show up at real discounts, and inventory turns over constantly, making it a solid stop for anyone still figuring out how to source products to sell online . Understanding the Nordstrom Rack return policy before you source is the risk variable you can't ignore. If an item doesn't sell and you're past 30 to 40 days, you own it outright. Most resale timelines, especially for anything niche or off-season, run longer than that, so sourcing decisions need to account for the clock and not just the discount. Final sale items carry the highest risk of all. There's no recourse if a piece sits unsold for months or turns out to be a poor fit for your buyer base. Give it a second look before you commit to anything marked final sale, no matter how good the price looks. One thing that trips up newer resellers: Rack items often carry a Rack-specific price tag stapled or looped alongside the brand's own tag, and buyers on different resale platforms have different expectations about which tags stay on and which get removed before listing. Get that wrong and you'll field messages about it. If you're sourcing across Nordstrom Rack, TJ Maxx, Marshalls, and Saks Off 5th in the same week, keeping the TJ Maxx return policy and the Marshalls return policy straight alongside Rack's own windows adds up to real operational friction. Final Thoughts Know your window: 30 days for in-store purchases, 40 days from the ship date for anything bought online. Keep your proof of purchase somewhere you can actually find it, and check for the final sale label before you commit, especially on clearance racks where it's stamped in small print. None of this is complicated once you know it. The Nordstrom Rack return policy is entirely workable for shoppers who buy with intention rather than expecting to change their minds later. The friction only shows up for people expecting the open-ended flexibility that full-line Nordstrom offers. Return windows can vary by season, so bookmark the official nordstromrack.com policy page and check it before you buy rather than relying on what worked last year. Frequently asked questions Can I return Nordstrom Rack items to a regular Nordstrom store? No. Nordstrom Rack and full-line Nordstrom run separate return systems, so items bought at Rack have to go back to a Rack store or through Rack's own online return process. The same rule applies in reverse: purchases made at full-line Nordstrom can't be returned to a Rack location. Bring Rack purchases to a physical Rack store or start an online return at nordstromrack.com. What happens if I return something to Nordstrom Rack without a receipt? Without a receipt, order confirmation, or order number, the return is up to the store manager's discretion. When it's approved, you'll typically get store credit at the item's lowest recorded selling price rather than a refund to your original payment method. Bringing any proof of purchase, even a confirmation email, speeds up the process and avoids relying on a manager's judgment call. Are Nordstrom Rack final sale items ever returnable? No. Final sale items are non-returnable with no exceptions, even if the item is defective. A defect claim goes through customer service as a separate process rather than a standard return, and the final sale label shows up on both the product page and your receipt before you buy. How long does a Nordstrom Rack refund take to hit my account? In-store returns post to credit or debit cards in 3 to 5 business days, and cash refunds are immediate. Mailed returns take 5 to 7 business days for the warehouse to process once your package arrives, then another 3 to 5 business days for the refund to reach your card. Dropping off an online order at a physical Rack store instead of mailing it speeds up the whole process. Does Nordstrom Rack extend its return window during the holidays? Sometimes. Rack has loosened return windows for November and December purchases in past years, but the extension isn't guaranteed annually. Check the official nordstromrack.com policy page each holiday season to confirm the current terms before you buy or return gifts.

title: 41 companies in Germany that sponsor work visas in 2026
summary: Hoping to work in Germany? Here are 41 companies known to sponsor work visas in 2026, how the skilled worker route and Blue Card work, and how to apply.
body_text: Germany is one of the best countries to move to as a professional. Despite the country’s economic prowess, they still face shortages in technology, engineering, healthcare, logistics, and manufacturing. This creates a unique opportunity for eligible Nigerians and other African professionals to fill in the gaps. Germany sponsors foreign professionals through the skilled worker visa and the EU Blue Card, both of which require a qualifying job offer. Employers in engineering, IT, healthcare and manufacturing regularly hire from abroad. The Blue Card requires a recognised degree and a salary above a set threshold. This guide explains how the sponsorship process works, which companies are known to hire from abroad, and what to expect once you arrive. How work visa sponsorship works in Germany Unlike countries such as the UK , Germany doesn’t have a formal register of licensed sponsors. There is one official list of companies that can sponsor foreign workers. Instead, any company in Germany can hire someone outside the EU if the role meets the visa requirements, and the employer is willing to go through the process. Usually, large companies and multinationals already have international recruitment teams familiar with the process. There are two relevant visa routes for skilled workers. For a full explanation of visa options and living in Germany as a foreigner, see our Germany digital nomad and expat work visa guide . The skilled worker visa This option is available to non-EU citizens who have a recognised qualification (degree or vocational qualification) and a valid job offer from a German employer. Your qualifications must generally be recognised in Germany, and the job should match your training or experience. Salary requirements depend on the occupation and current immigration rules rather than a single fixed threshold. The employer does not need to demonstrate that no EU candidate was available (as is required in some countries, including Luxembourg ), but the role must align with the applicant's qualifications. Full details on requirements are available at Make It In Germany . The EU Blue Card An EU Blue Card is the juicy route, but more difficult. It offers a faster path to permanent residence, easier family reunification, and the ability to move and work within the EU. This option is designed for highly qualified professionals with a recognised university degree and a job offer that meets the minimum salary requirement. In 2026, the minimum annual gross salary is approximately €48,300 for most professions and around €43,760 for recognised shortage occupations, including IT, engineering, mathematics, natural sciences, and healthcare (subject to annual updates). With the EU Blue Card, you can move to other EU countries after 18 months, and you can become a permanent resident after 21 months, especially if you have good German language skills. 41 companies in Germany that sponsor work visas Many German employers actively recruit international talent, particularly in sectors facing skills shortages such as engineering, healthcare, manufacturing, finance, and information technology. The companies below have a history of hiring skilled professionals from outside the EU and supporting them through the work visa or EU Blue Card process. While these employers regularly recruit internationally, sponsorship depends on the role, your qualifications, and the company's current hiring needs. Always check the employer's careers page and confirm that the position is open to international applicants before applying. managers Zalando E-commerce Software engineers, data scientists, product managers HelloFresh Food technology Engineers, data analysts, operations specialists Delivery Hero Food delivery technology Software engineers, product managers While these employers regularly recruit internationally, sponsorship depends on the role, your qualifications, and the company's current hiring needs. Always check the employer's careers page and confirm that the position is open to international applicants before applying, and ask specifically whether they sponsor the skilled worker visa or Blue Card. Industries most likely to sponsor Germany is experiencing labour shortages across several sectors, making it easier for qualified international professionals to secure jobs with visa sponsorship. If you have experience in one of these fields, your chances of finding an employer willing to hire from abroad are significantly higher. IT and software: Software engineers, data scientists, cloud architects, and cybersecurity professionals. Engineering: Mechanical, electrical, civil, and aerospace engineers with recognised qualifications and German or English communication skills are in high demand. Healthcare: Doctors, nurses, dentists, physiotherapists, and other healthcare workers. They might need to write the appropriate qualifying exam. Clinical roles generally require German language proficiency, often at the B2 level or above. Manufacturing and production: Skilled trades, process engineers, and quality management specialists are in demand in the chemicals, automotive, and food production sectors. How to apply for a sponsored role in Germany Finding an employer willing to sponsor your work visa requires more than simply submitting applications. Following the right process improves your chances of success. Step 1: Get your qualifications recognised Germany requires many foreign qualifications to be recognised before a work visa can be issued. Use the official ANABIN database or the Recognition in Germany portal to verify whether your degree or vocational qualification is recognised. Regulated professions such as medicine, nursing, pharmacy, and teaching usually require additional recognition from the relevant German authority before you can begin work. Step 2: Find roles on the right platforms Focus on employers that regularly recruit international talent. Good places to search include: LinkedIn Jobs StepStone Germany Indeed Germany Make it in Germany Job Exchange Company careers pages Where it is possible, filter for roles that explicitly mention "sponsorship" or "relocation support”. Most large companies accept applications in English even for roles that eventually need you to learn some German. Step 3: Tailor your CV to German standards German employers expect a detailed CV that clearly outlines your qualifications and work experience. Your application should usually include: A professional CV A tailored cover letter ( Anschreiben ) Copies of relevant qualifications Professional certifications where applicable Unlike UK CVs, German CVs commonly include a professional photograph and personal details such as your date of birth, although this is becoming less common at international companies. Step 4: Receive a job offer Once you successfully complete the interview process, your employer issues a formal employment contract. If you're applying for an EU Blue Card, your salary must meet the applicable threshold. For the Skilled Worker visa, your qualification must generally be recognised and relevant to the position offered. Step 5: Apply for your visa and wait Submit your visa application through the German embassy or consulate in your country. The documents they commonly ask for include: Valid passport Signed employment contract Qualification recognition documents Completed visa application form Biometric photographs Proof of health insurance (where required) Any additional documents requested by the embassy Processing usually takes between six and twelve weeks, although timelines vary depending on your country and profession. Step 6: Register your address and settle in After arriving, you must register your address ( Anmeldung ) with the local registration office, usually within 14 days. You'll also need to: Obtain your tax identification number, Open a German bank account, Register for health insurance (if applicable), and Resume your job. Getting paid in euros and sending money home Most employers in Germany pay salaries monthly in euros by bank transfer. Your payslip will show deductions such as income tax ( Lohnsteuer ), health insurance, pension contributions, unemployment insurance, and long-term care insurance. Depending on your income and tax class, total deductions are typically between 35% and 45% of your gross salary. Once you are earning in euros, you will likely want to send money home. UK age assurance regulations are evolving rapidly, requiring businesses to implement reliable systems to verify user age. The increasing use of Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) complicates this, as they can mask a user's true location, making age verification more challenging. The Evolving Landscape of UK Age Assurance The United Kingdom has been at the forefront of establishing stringent age assurance standards, particularly for online services. This is driven by a commitment to protect children from harmful content and interactions. Key legislation and guidance include the Age Appropriate Design Code (AADC) and the forthcoming Online Safety Act (OSA). Age Appropriate Design Code (AADC) Introduced by the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the AADC sets out 15 standards that online services likely to be accessed by children must meet. While not explicitly about age verification, it mandates that services understand their user base and apply appropriate protections. This often necessitates age assurance to segment users and apply age-appropriate settings by default. Online Safety Act (OSA) The Online Safety Act, once fully implemented, will significantly strengthen age assurance requirements. It places a legal duty of care on online service providers to protect users, especially children, from illegal and harmful content. This includes specific obligations to prevent children from accessing age-inappropriate material, which will likely require reliable age verification and age estimation mechanisms. Deepfake attacks surged over 700% year-over-year, highlighting the escalating need for advanced identity verification and age assurance technologies. The Challenge of VPN Use in UK Age Assurance VPNs are widely used for privacy, security, and accessing geo-restricted content. However, they pose a significant hurdle for businesses attempting to comply with UK age assurance regulations. A VPN can mask a user's true IP address, making it appear as if they are accessing a service from a different country or region. This can lead to several problems: Location Spoofing: A minor in the UK could use a VPN to appear as if they are in a country with less stringent age restrictions, bypassing local controls. False Positives/Negatives: Legitimate adult users in the UK might be incorrectly flagged or denied access if their VPN makes their location ambiguous. Bypassing Geo-blocking: Age-restricted content providers often rely on IP-based geo-blocking, which VPNs can circumvent. To effectively implement UK age assurance with VPNs in mind, businesses need to move beyond simple IP-based checks and adopt more sophisticated, multi-layered strategies. Strategies for Effective UK Age Assurance with VPNs Achieving reliable UK age assurance while accounting for VPN usage requires a combination of technical measures and policy considerations. No single method is foolproof, so a layered approach is essential. Multi-Factor Age Verification Relying solely on IP analysis is insufficient when VPNs are prevalent. Businesses should integrate multiple verification methods: Document Verification This involves users uploading an official government-issued ID (e.g., passport, driving license). Advanced ID verification solutions can extract data, check for tampering, and verify authenticity. Didit's iBeta Level 1 certified liveness detection helps prevent spoofing attacks. Age Estimation AI-powered age estimation from a selfie can provide an initial assessment or a fallback mechanism. While not definitive for strict age gates, it can flag users who are clearly underage, prompting further verification. This information, combined with other fraud signals, can inform risk scores and trigger additional verification steps. Didit's IP Analysis module offers silent background checks. Data-Driven Risk Assessment Implement a dynamic risk-based approach. If a user is detected using a VPN, their risk score increases, prompting more rigorous age verification steps. This could mean escalating from age estimation to full document and biometric checks. This adaptive approach ensures a balance between user experience and compliance. Don’t forget to ask questions. Of course, ask if there are any rebates, lease deals, specials, and incentives to lease your next vehicle. Ask if there is added flexibility with any given offer. When it comes to leasing, this could mean asking for a higher milage cap, or seeing if there is any wiggle room on the amount of the down payment to come up with a specific monthly payment. If you’re someone who likes to have more cash in-hand when doing the deal, a lower down payment could offset the uptick in future monthly payments .
